insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Individual/Family Floater: 5L to 3Cr (by plan). Family First: Base individual SI 1L to 15L + floater SI as per formula (by plan).

great.name: Restore/Refill benefit (same & different illness) – up to 100% of Base Sum Insured
great.quote: Re-fill benefit Reinstate up to base Sum Insured. Applicable for same & different illness as well
great.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table; also Section 3.13 Re-fill Benefit
great.explanation: If your Base SI (and loyalty additions, if any) gets used up in a policy year, the insurer provides an additional amount up to 100% of Base SI for further eligible hospitalization claims in the same policy year.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 90 days
great.quote: We will pay above mentioned Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 90 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
great.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses incurred up to 90 days before hospitalization (subject to claim under inpatient/day care/domiciliary/modern treatments being accepted).

great.name: PED waiting period: 24 months
great.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage (industry-good, and treated as strong vs many policies offering 36 months).

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Standard initial waiting period for illnesses (accidents are covered from day 1).

good.name: Specific disease/procedure waiting period: 12 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 12 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Listed specific diseases/procedures are covered after 12 months (better than the common 24 months).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 180 days
good.quote: We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 180 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge (good market standard).

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization covered
good.quote: We will indemnify on Reimbursement basis only, the Medical Expenses incurred for the Insured Person’s Domiciliary Hospitalization during the Policy Period
good.explanation: Home treatment is covered when medically required and subject to conditions (e.g., minimum 3 consecutive days).

good.name: Modern treatments covered but with sub-limits on certain robotic surgeries
good.quote: Modern Treatments Covered up to Sum Insured with sub-limit of Rs. 1Lac on few robotic surgeries
good.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table; also Section 3.25 (Modern Treatments) special condition
good.explanation: Modern treatments are included; however, certain robotic surgeries have a ₹1 lakh cap (except listed exceptions).

good.name: NCB/Renewal Bonus present but resets on claim (cumulative bonus as loyalty additions)
good.quote: We will provide Loyalty Additions in the form of Cumulative Bonus by increasing the Sum Insured applicable under the Policy by 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the immediately preceding Policy Year subject to a maximum of 100% of the Base Sum Insured.
good.explanation: Sum Insured can increase by 10% per year up to 100% (good), but the document does not state that this bonus is protected/non-reducing after claims—so treat as standard NCB behavior.

good.name: Optional add-on: Enhanced Loyalty Additions (higher NCB) available
good.quote: Loyalty Additions ... automatically increase to 20% of Base Insured and the maximum Loyalty Additions shall not exceed 200% of the Base Sum Insured.
good.explanation: Optional paid cover to increase renewal bonus accrual and maximum cap (a flexibility feature, not a restriction).

bad.name: Room rent (Family First – Silver): daily cap (rupee capping)
bad.quote: Room rent Option 1: Rs 3,000 per day or Shared Room; whichever is lower Option 2: Rs 5,000 per day or Single Private Room; whichever is lower
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table (Family First variant – Silver)
bad.explanation: A fixed daily room-rent cap can lead to proportionate deductions on the entire bill if you take a higher-category room than allowed.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applies when room category is higher than eligibility in policy schedule
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the room category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligibility as specified in the Policy Schedule, then We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses ...
bad.explanation: If your allowed room category is capped (as in some variants/plans), choosing a higher room can reduce payable amounts across associated expenses (room, nursing, doctor fees, OT charges) via pro-rating.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (many common items explicitly non-payable)
bad.quote: Annexure VII - The expenses that are not covered ... List  I – Expenses not covered ... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Annexure VII – The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges / procedure charges / costs of treatment
bad.explanation: Many consumables/items (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit, various kits) are listed as not payable/subsumed, which commonly results in out-of-pocket expenses.

bad.name: Mandatory co-pay if Zone 2 is chosen: 20% in listed geographies
bad.quote: If You select Zone 2, then 20% Co-payment will apply for treatment in Mumbai (including Navi Mumbai & Thane), Delhi NCR, Kolkata & Gujarat State.
bad.explanation: If you opt for Zone 2 pricing, a 20% co-pay applies for treatment in the specified locations. This is a meaningful cost share and can reduce claim payout.

bad.name: Disease/benefit sub-limits exist (examples: HIV, mental disorders, robotic surgery cap)
bad.quote: HIV / AIDS covered up to Rs 50,000 ... Mental disorder treatment ... (sub-limit of Rs 50,000 applicable on few conditions) ... Modern Treatments ... sub-limit of Rs. 1Lac on few robotic surgeries
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table; Section 3.17; Section 3.19; Section 3.25
bad.explanation: The policy includes multiple sub-limits on specific conditions/benefits, which can create higher out-of-pocket costs for those categories.

unclear.name: Co-pay (default/base plan) not explicitly stated as 0% or not; depends on schedule/zone selection
unclear.quote: Co-payment (if applicable) as specified in the Policy Schedule shall be applicable on the amount payable by Us.
unclear.explanation: The wording says co-pay applies if mentioned in the Policy Schedule and also has a Zone 2 co-pay rule. For your exact policy, confirm from the policy schedule whether any co-pay applies by default (apart from optional Zone 2 choice).

unclear.name: Cashless network size not specified
unclear.quote: Cashless Facility can be availed only at Our Network Providers or Service Providers (as applicable). The complete list of Network Providers is available on Our website
unclear.explanation: The document does not state the number of network hospitals. Verify the current network count and hospitals in your city from the insurer’s website/app.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
